author: Sean Hollister
description:
On Tuesday, defense contractor Anduril and chipmaker Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States, starting with a single model in 2027. They also announced a "long-term goal" of pushing the computer industry to create "a fully domestic supply chain."

Even a single Made-in-USA laptop would be a surprise, because no major US computer company builds its laptops here - not Apple, not Dell, not HP, not Micr
title: Anduril now says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch

author: Stevie Bonifield
description: Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don't like AI, and it's not just young people and creatives. Appearing on the Colin and Samir podcast to talk about the launch of widescreen and long-form video for Instagram, Mosseri said he thin
title: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’

author: Emma Roth
description: A hacker stole a trove of personal information from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The breach exposes the names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses, and office locations of more than 41,000 employees, including those in US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), according to TechCrunch and
title: A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records

author: Terrence O’Brien
description: The MPC Sample Key isn't even formally announced yet, but Akai is already showing off what the modding community is cooking up through vibe coding. Akai has decided to embrace the explosion of hackers and custom firmware developers by giving them early access to the device, which will have open-source firmware.
title: Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC

author: David Pierce
description:
For the last several years, Readwise has been building tools for power readers. There's the eponymous product, Readwise, which stores and categorizes your Kindle highlights to help you remember what you've read. There's Readwise Reader, an app for reading newsletters, PDFs, and web articles you've saved for later. And now there's Readwise Books, a full-fledged platform for buying, reading, and talking about books.

Readwise Books is currently in beta, availabl
title: Readwise is taking on Kindle and Kobo for ebook supremacy

author: Jay Peters
description:
Google parent company Alphabet says that its AI investments are leading to a big growth in searches year-over-year, as noted in its Q3 2026 earnings today.

"Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries," CEO Sundar Pichai says in a statement. "In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it's been in the last five years."
title: Google says its investments in AI are driving more searches

author: Andrew Liszewski
description: With an OLED display and touchscreen capabilities, it's no surprise that the new MacBook Pro Apple announced today is more expensive than the MBP announced earlier this year. But upgrading the base models that start at $2,899 for the 14-inch, and $3,399 for the 16-inch, with every premium hardwar
title: Apple charges $14,549 for a fully specced touchscreen MacBook Pro

author: Emma Roth
description:
Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, offering "significant gains" in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In an announcement on Wednesday, Google highlights Carbon's top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind.

The new Gemini 4 Carbon model offers impro
title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity

author: Sean Hollister
description: What do drones, routers, and Roombas have in common? The US government wants to keep Chinese ones from entering the country. They’re the first consu
title: Foreign gadget bans: all the news about the FCC’s clampdown on Chinese tech

author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
description:
Apple announced a new iPad Mini with a larger OLED display this week, and we've just gotten to try it out at Apple's "Pro and tell" event.

It's an iPad for sure, but the new OLED on the Mini looks exceptional, and the optional nano-texture matte finish is awesome. The "Pro and tell" event venue has soft lighting that's not the most conducive to blinding glare on displays, but the matte finish pretty much squashes it entirely.

Moving the front-facing camer
title: Hands-on with the new OLED iPad Mini

author: Stevie Bonifield
description: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr announced the agency will vote on November 19th on rules that would allow prisons to use signal jamming. Radiofrequency jammers are generally banned under Section 333 and the Communications Act of 1934, with few exceptions, and Carr has noted they've been permitted for use at some federal facilities already. Carr claims in a statement that jammers are needed because "For years, thousands upon thousands of contraband cellphones have been pouring into prisons, and some of the worst possib
title: Brendan Carr plans to let prisons jam cellphone signals

author: Andrew Liszewski
description: Nearly two years after LG and Samsung announced at CES 2025 that their latest smart TVs would include access to Microsoft's Copilot, the company is ending support for the AI assistant's functionality on all TVs this year, according to a report by Windows Central.
title: Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs

author: Sean Hollister
description:
In this economy, how often does a product get less expensive before its debut? That just happened with the Google / Xreal Aura, the lightweight 95-gram glasses with a tethered Android XR compute puck and multiple virtual screens that just went on sale today. Xreal and Google have just announced the headset costs $1,099 through the end of the year, down from the $1,279 that Xreal was charging for early preorders last month.

I expect that's because
title: Surprise: The Google Xreal glasses debut at a Meta-beating $1,099

author: Brad Bourque
description: As expected, Apple finally showed off its 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros at its recent "Pro and Tell" event. The long-awaited laptops feature a Tandem OLED display with full touch capabilities, while also cutting some weight and bringing back the glowing Apple logo. While less exciting, there's also an updated 14-inch MacBook Pro that features Apple's M6 CPU, along with
title: Here’s where to preorder the new MacBook Pros

description: This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer

author: Allison Johnson
description:
Touchscreen laptops are nothing new in the Windows world, but Apple has only just announced its first MacBook with a touchscreen. Apple isn't rushing to change a bunch of things in macOS to optimize for touch, though; most of the touch action will be in the apps themselves, it seems.

As far as major macOS changes go, iOS's Dynamic Island will be debuting on the new MacBook Pro, and Apple touts the added touch controls as particularly useful for interacting with the interface to
title: Here’s how macOS is changing for touchscreens

author: Emma Roth
description:
Apple closed out its week of product announcements with a "Pro and Tell" event on Wednesday, where it took the wraps off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro. Though Apple may have saved its biggest and most exciting update for last, it revealed a few other device upgrades and updates in the days leading up to its big reveal. We've rounded them all up here.

A MacBook Pro with a touchscreen
title: Apple ‘Pro and Tell’ event: everything announced this week

author: Stevie Bonifield
description: Apple just announced its first touchscreen MacBook at its "Pro and tell" event on Wednesday. It showed off the long-awaited touchscreen in a video of the new MacBook Pro during the event that you can watch right here to see the new display in action.
title: Watch Apple’s reveal video for the touchscreen MacBook Pro

author: Terrence O’Brien
description: Steve Jobs famously called touchscreen laptops "ergonomically terrible," and for over a decade, Apple stridently refused to make one. Today that all changes with the MacBook Pro - the company's first laptop to embrace a touch interface. While it's unlikely that Apple can fix all the "terrible" ergonomics of hav
title: Hands-on with Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro

author: Sheena Vasani
description: Apple's smallest tablet is getting a bigger screen. Earlier this week, the company announced the eighth-generation iPad Mini alongside several new MacBook Pro models, bringing OLED technology to Apple's miniature tablet for the first time. The diminutive slate won't hit shelves until November 6th; however, you can already preorder it from Amazon,
title: Here’s where you can preorder the new OLED-equipped iPad Mini

author: Jess Weatherbed
description: Instagram is testing long-form videos (again) to lure in creatives from YouTube, but the platform hasn't figured out how (or if) it'll actually pay them. After Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced Features on Monday, creators immediately started voicing their complaints on Thre
title: Instagram doesn’t have a plan to pay long-form video creators

author: Jay Peters
description:
Apple announced an all-new MacBook Pro laptop with an OLED touchscreen at its "Pro and tell" event on Wednesday. It starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model, or $3,399 for the 16-inch version, and it's available to preorder today ahead of its release on November 6th.

The new MacBook Pro has what Apple calls a "PROLED XDR" display, which is a tandem OLED screen. It offers up to 2,000 nits of peak SDR brightness, up to a 120Hz refresh rate, and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. It's equ
title: Apple announces its first touchscreen MacBook Pro

author: Andrew Liszewski
description: Following improvements made to Chrome's enhanced autofill last year that included your name, passport number, email address, and physical addresses sourced from your Google Accounts and services like Google Wallet, the feature is now expanding. Starting today, Chrome's enhanced autofill will use Gemini with Personal Intelligence to suggest information sourced from your G
title: Chrome’s enhanced autofill can now pull info from Gmail to help you fill out forms

author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
description: Apple has already had a busy week. On Monday, it announced a new iPad Mini with an upgraded OLED display</
title: Touchscreen MacBook live blog: On the ground at Apple’s launch event

author: Stevie Bonifield
description:
Apple’s “Pro and tell” event kicks off at 1PM ET / 10AM PT on October 28th. The event comes just a couple of weeks after Apple debuted the HomeView, its first smart display, and a little over a month after it announced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable. Its next event could feature yet another first for Apple: a MacBook with a touchscreen.

A few devices received updates in the days leading up to the event. Apple announced
title: All the news from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event

author: Emma Roth
description:
Meta says it may push the implementation of its new business terms past November 20th as it faces backlash from publishers over concerns about AI training. In a post on X, Meta communications head Andy Stone said the company does "not plan to make policy changes without a full consultation with industry groups and leaders."

The new business terms, which were supposed to take effect on October 30th, initially
title: Meta says it’ll probably delay its controversial new business terms again

author: Jay Peters
description:
Reddit is switching up its homepage feeds. The company announced today that it's going to start offering a "new feed experience" that includes both a Following feed to show you posts from subreddits you follow and a For You feed that includes posts from your subreddits and "recommendations related to your interests." You may already have the new feeds - I actually noticed them on my account yesterday.

It's a big shift for the platform, but not an entirely surprising one, as Reddit hasn't been shy abo
title: Reddit is getting a For You feed

author: Sheena Vasani
description: Halloween isn’t even here yet, but it’s never too early to start thinking about holiday decorations, especially when there are already deals on smart, programmable lights. If you want your house, tree, fireplace, or whatever else to stand out this year, Govee’s Christmas String Lights 2 are on sale starting at $74.99 ($25 off) at Amazon and directly from
title: Govee’s colorful smart string lights are down to their best price of the year

author: Andrew Liszewski
description:
Sony announced a new Prism Collection line of PlayStation 5 accessories today that revisits "the iconic see-through trend of the late '90s in a fresh, modern way" for its DualSense wireless controllers and matching console covers for the PS5 that reveal some of their internal components.

The Prism Collection is launching with three color options including flare orange, emerald green, and g
title: Sony has new transparent PS5 controllers launching next year

author: Brad Bourque
description: It's hard to make an Xbox controller that stands out these days, especially one that's expensive, due to a wealth of great semi-affordable options. Still, 8BitDo's $150 Ultimate 3E is a bold controller that holds its own against other feature-packed options. It's made for Xbox and PC gamers who want a deeper level of customization and a more refined design than
title: 8BitDo’s new Xbox Elite-style controller sets a high bar for customization

author: Stevie Bonifield
description:
The MacBook Neo now starts at $649 on Apple's Education Store, up $150 from its initial $499 education starting price. As reported earlier by MacRumors, the student discount for the Neo received a $50 price bump in recent days, following a $100 price bump back in June.

Apple's budget MacBook is now just $50 off its regular $699 starting price for students, rather than the usu
title: Apple raises the MacBook Neo’s student pricing again

author: Emma Roth
description: A subsidiary of Elon Musk's xAI is offering to buy up homes in a Mississippi neighborhood, as long as residents don't join a lawsuit targeting the company's nearby data center and power plant, according to a report from The Guardian. A realtor going door-to-door in the Southaven neighborhood rep
title: xAI is buying out homeowners who promise not to sue over data center noise

author: Stevie Bonifield
description: Virgin Galactic's new spaceship is here, dubbed "Apeiron" by popular vote from a public poll. Apeiron is the first of the company's new Delta-class spacecraft, but it isn't slated to launch for nearly another year. Earlier this week, Virgin Galactic
title: Here’s Virgin Galactic’s new Apeiron spaceship

author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
description: Amazon swapped its usual big fall hardware showcase this year for a series of smaller launches throughout October. So far this month, it has announced new Fire TV devices, new Kindles, the Alexa Tablet Pro 12,
title: Inside Amazon’s Echo hardware event

author: Cameron Faulkner
description:
Amazon used to blast out dozens of products onstage at annual hardware events. If this October is any indication, the company has wisely changed its strategy to put more focus on each new product with its own launch. The latest round of launches focuses on Echo products, including speakers, smart displays, as well as a smart photo frame.

All products, save for the new Echo Show 16 (which might be the most interesting of the bunch), are available to buy today. This includes the
title: Almost all of Amazon’s new Echo gear is available now

author: Jess Weatherbed
description:
Amazon had plenty of new gadgets to share at its Echo hardware event this year, along with updates to the AI-powered Alexa Plus after it became available to everyone in the US in February. But the big news this year is screens: devices with big, beautiful ones, and those that lack them entirely.

There’s the Alexa Photo Frame, which Amazon devices chief Panos Panay describes as “the world’s smartest photo frame” and that doubles as a full Alexa speaker. There’s also t
title: Everything announced at Amazon’s October 2026 hardware launch

author: Emma Roth
description:
Amazon has just taken the wraps off a bunch of new devices as part of a string of fall announcements. Today's news focuses largely on new Echo speakers, with a few new smart home gadgets sprinkled in.

Here's a roundup of all of the updates Amazon revealed on Wednesday.
title: Amazon’s new Echo line is here: the 6 biggest updates

author: Jess Weatherbed
description: Amazon's smart home map interface that shows you where all your connected devices are has been overhauled with new graphics, features, and dynamic effects. The new Alexa Home Map is now an interactive 3D view of not just everything that's inside your property, but outside of it too - u
title: Amazon’s Alexa Home Map is getting a smarter 3D redesign

author: Andrew Liszewski
description: Amazon's screen-equipped smart speakers have long been able to display your family's photos, but its new Alexa Photo Frame is purpose-built for that task. It's designed to compete with other digital picture frames from companies like Aura, and Amazon's incorporates a smart speaker with access to Alexa Plus' capabilities through voice commands. However, unlike the Echo Show and Amazon's other smart home hubs, the Alexa Photo Frame only ever displays your photos, and you'll never be served an ad.
title: Amazon’s first digital picture frame lets you add voice notes to photos

author: Jay Peters
description:
Amazon is giving its premium smart speaker a camera. The new Echo Studio with Home Camera, announced today as part of Amazon's big blast of announcements, has a built-in camera for monitoring a room while you're away, showing things to Alexa, and, soon, to use with video calls on Fire TV devices. It's an iteration on the revised Echo Studio announced last year, which had a brand-new design.

The Echo Studio with Home Camera also offers some audio updates. Amazon says a new feature called "Advanced Room Adaptation" will continuously tune sound to the space that the speaker is in. There's also an "Ad
title: Amazon’s new Echo Studio speaker has a camera

author: Lauren Feiner
description:
Kroger's $1.65 billion proposed acquisition of Giant Eagle might not only consolidate the grocery market, but also a vast surveillance network that includes Flock cameras, a new report warns.

Beyond standard concerns that a merger could decrease competition and increase prices, the American Econ
title: How a grocery merger could expand a surveillance network

author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
description: Amazon just announced its newest smart alarm clock - the Echo Time. The baseball-sized smart speaker with a screen, the Time looks like an Echo Dot with Clock and an Echo Spot had a much bigger baby. It features a 3.2-inch touchscreen that prominently displays your choice of a huge selection of clockfaces and includes a sleep-sensing feature that promises to rouse you at just the right time in your sleep cycle to help you feel more rested. It costs $199
title: Spending time with the Echo Time — a smart clock that senses you sleeping

author: Justine Calma
description:
Ask Texas NAACP president Gary Bledsoe what it's been like to see data center developers descend upon Austin and its surrounding suburbs and he can rattle off project after project facing opposition from locals.

There's the fight in Taylor over plans to build a data center at a site that's supposed to be a park. Temple, around 40 miles away, is another sore s
title: Voters in Texas agree: They hate data centers
